card.summary_ko: 1895년 1월 7일 고종이 종묘에서 서약한 14개 조의 개혁 강령으로, 청에 대한 의존을 끊고 왕실과 국정을 분리하며 재정·조세·군제·법제를 정비한다는 갑오개혁의 기본 문서이다.
card.summary_en: The Fourteen Articles of the Grand Plan, sworn by King Gojong at the Royal Ancestral Shrine on 7 January 1895: the basic charter of the Gabo reforms, breaking dependence on Qing and setting out reforms of court, finance, taxation, army and law.
card.edition_ko: 洪範十四條 — 중국어 위키문헌, 판 2590162 (《관보》 판 한 벌만 수록; 《고종실록》 간체자 사본은 제외); 원문은 공문서(저작권법 제7조)로 보호 대상이 아니며, 전사는 위키문헌 기여자(CC BY-SA 4.0)

notes.ko:
**저자 (발행 주체)** 이 글은 고종(1852–1919)이 종묘에서 읽은 서고문과 홍범 14조로, 공식적으로는 고종의 이름으로 발표되었다. 실제로는 갑오개혁을 이끈 제2차 김홍집 내각(김홍집·박영효 연립)이 일본공사 이노우에 가오루의 조언과 압력 속에서 마련한 것으로 알려져 있다. 김홍집(1842–1896)은 온건 개화파 관료로 총리대신을 지냈고 1896년 아관파천 직후 군중에게 살해되었다. 박영효(1861–1939)는 1884년 갑신정변을 주도한 급진 개화파로, 일본 망명 뒤 1894년 귀국해 내무대신이 되었고 1910년 병합 뒤 일본 정부로부터 후작 작위(조선귀족)를 받아 친일인명사전에 올라 있다. 유길준 등 개화파가 기초에 참여했다고 전해진다. 이 개혁 세력은 근대화를 추구했지만 일본군의 주둔과 영향 아래에 있었다는 점이 평가를 갈리게 한다.

**시대적 맥락** 1894년 동학농민운동 뒤 청일전쟁이 일어나자 일본은 경복궁을 점령하고 개화파 정권을 세웠다(제1차 갑오개혁, 군국기무처). 같은 해 10월 이노우에가 공사로 부임하고 12월 김홍집·박영효 연립내각이 서면서 제2차 개혁이 시작되었다. 고종은 개국 503년 12월 12일(양력 1895년 1월 7일) 종묘에 나아가 서고문을 읽고 14개 조를 선서했다. 이어 청일전쟁에서 일본이 이겨 1895년 4월 시모노세키 조약 제1조가 조선의 독립을 확인했고, 10월 을미사변과 이후 단발령, 1896년 2월 아관파천과 김홍집 내각의 붕괴가 잇달았다.

**배경** 이 판본은 중국어 위키문헌 「洪範十四條」에서 《관보》 판(서고문과 14조) 한 벌만 싣는다. 같은 면에 있는 《고종실록》의 간체자 사본은 중복이므로 뺐다. 위키문헌 머리글은 1899년 8월 17일 대한국 국제가 반포되면서 효력이 끝난 것으로 적고 있다.

**의의** 제1조 "청에 대한 의존의 생각을 끊고 자주독립의 기초를 세운다"가 첫머리에 있다. 왕실 사무와 국정의 분리(제4조), 조세 법정주의(제6조), 재정의 탁지아문 일원화(제7조), 예산 제도(제9조), 해외 유학생 파견(제11조), 징병제(제12조), 민법·형법의 제정과 인신 보호(제13조), 문벌에 얽매이지 않는 인재 등용(제14조)이 담겼다. 근대적 국가 체제의 청사진이지만 실제 시행은 제한적이었다.

**형식과 주제** 서고문(조상에게 올리는 맹세)과 14조로 이루어진 한문이다. 관보 판은 14조가 한 문단으로 이어져 있고 '大君主'나 '祖宗' 앞에서 칸을 띄우는 격식이 보인다.

**읽기 도움**
- 誓告文(서고문): 조상에게 맹세하며 고하는 글
- 洪範(홍범): 큰 규범
- 自主獨立(자주독립): 스스로 서서 남에게 속하지 않음
- 大君主(대군주): 개국 503년 무렵의 조선 국왕 호칭
- 王室典範(왕실전범): 왕실의 법
- 度支衙門(탁지아문): 재정 담당 관청
- 議政府(의정부): 최고 행정 기관
- 徵兵法(징병법): 징병에 관한 법
- 人才登庸(인재등용): 인재를 뽑아 씀
notes.en:
**About the author (issuing authority)** This is the oath text read by Gojong (1852-1919) at the Royal Ancestral Shrine and the Fourteen Articles, officially issued in his name. In practice they are understood to have been prepared by the second Kim Hong-jip cabinet (a Kim Hong-jip and Bak Yeong-hyo coalition), which led the Gabo reforms, under the advice and pressure of the Japanese minister Inoue Kaoru. Kim Hong-jip (1842-1896) was a moderate reformist official who served as prime minister and was killed by a crowd in 1896 after the king's flight to the Russian legation. Bak Yeong-hyo (1861-1939) was a radical reformer who led the 1884 Gapsin coup, returned from exile in Japan in 1894 to become Home Minister, and after the 1910 annexation received a marquis title from the Japanese government (as a Korean peer) and is listed in the Dictionary of Pro-Japanese Collaborators. Reformers such as Yu Gil-jun are said to have taken part in drafting. This reform camp sought modernisation but worked under Japanese troops and influence, which is why assessments differ.

**Historical context** After the 1894 Donghak uprising and the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese War, Japan seized Gyeongbokgung and installed a reformist government (first Gabo reforms, the Deliberative Council). Inoue took up his post in October, and in December the Kim Hong-jip and Bak Yeong-hyo coalition started the second stage of reform. On the 12th day of the 12th month of the 503rd year of the dynasty (7 January 1895) Gojong went to the shrine, read the oath and swore to the Fourteen Articles. Japan then won the war and Article 1 of the Treaty of Shimonoseki (April 1895) confirmed Joseon's independence; the Eulmi incident of October 1895, the topknot edict, the king's flight to the Russian legation in February 1896 and the fall of the Kim Hong-jip cabinet followed.

**Background** This edition is taken from Chinese Wikisource's "洪範十四條" and shows only one copy, the Official Gazette version (oath and articles). The duplicate copy of the Gojong Veritable Records on the same page, in simplified characters, is left out. The Wikisource header says the articles lost effect when the Daehanguk Gukje was promulgated on 17 August 1899.

**Significance** Article 1 comes first: "sever the thought of relying on Qing and firmly build the foundations of independence". Others separate court affairs from affairs of state (Art. 4), set taxes by law (Art. 6), concentrate finance in the finance office (Art. 7), introduce budgeting (Art. 9), send students abroad (Art. 11), adopt conscription (Art. 12), draw up civil and criminal codes and protect persons (Art. 13), and employ talent regardless of family status (Art. 14). They are a blueprint for a modern state, but implementation was limited.

**Form and themes** Classical Chinese consisting of an oath to the ancestors and fourteen articles. In the Gazette version the articles run together in one paragraph and there is the traditional spacing before honorific terms such as 大君主 and 祖宗.

**Reading help**
- 誓告文: a text of oath announced to the ancestors
- 洪範 (hongbeom): grand plan, great norm
- 自主獨立: self-rule and independence
- 大君主: "Grand Sovereign", the king's title around the year 503
- 王室典範: royal house code
- 度支衙門: finance office
- 議政府: State Council
- 徵兵法: conscription law
- 人才登庸: employing talent

paragraphs.orig: ## 大君主　展謁　宗廟誓告文
paragraphs.en: ## The Grand Sovereign's visit to the Ancestral Shrine: the text of the oath-announcement

paragraphs.orig: 維開國五百三年十二月十二日　　　　敢昭告于 皇祖列聖之靈惟朕小子粵自沖年嗣守我 祖宗丕丕基迄今三十有一載惟敬畏于天亦惟我 祖宗時式時依屢遭多難不荒墜厥緖朕小子其敢曰克享天心亶由我 祖宗眷顧騭佑惟皇我 祖肇造我王家啓我後人歷有五百三年逮朕之世時運丕變人文開暢友邦謀忠廷議協同惟自主獨立迺厥鞏固我國家朕小子曷敢不奉若天時以保我 祖宗遺業曷敢不奮發淬勵以增光我前人烈繼時自今毋他邦是恃恢國步于隆昌造生民之福祉以鞏固自主獨立之基念厥道毋或泥于舊毋狃于恬嬉惠迪我 祖宗宏謨監察宇內形勢釐革內政矯厥積弊朕小子玆將十四條洪範誓告我 祖宗在天之靈仰藉 祖宗之遺烈克底于績罔或敢違惟 明靈降鑑
paragraphs.en: In the 503rd year of the founding of the dynasty, the 12th month, the 12th day, I dare to make announcement to the spirits of the Imperial Ancestors and the successive sages. I, the little son, have since my childhood inherited and guarded the great foundations of Our Ancestors, for thirty-one years until now. I have been reverent toward Heaven, and have also followed Our Ancestors in all things; though I have encountered many troubles, I have not let the work fall into ruin. How could I, the little son, dare to say that I could enjoy the favour of Heaven? It is wholly through the care and protection of Our Ancestors. Our Imperial Ancestor first created this royal house and opened the way for later generations, for five hundred and three years in all; and in my generation the times have greatly changed, human culture has opened out, friendly states counsel us in good faith, and the deliberations of the court agree: only self-rule and independence can make our state secure. How could I, the little son, dare not to obey the season of Heaven and so preserve the legacy of Our Ancestors? How could I dare not to rouse myself and strive to add lustre to the achievements of my predecessors? From this time on I will not rely on other states, but will enlarge the nation's fortunes into prosperity and create the happiness of the people, so as to make firm the foundation of self-rule and independence. Reflecting on this way, I will not be bound by the old, nor grow used to ease and idleness, but follow the grand designs of Our Ancestors, observe the conditions of the world, reform internal government and correct its long-standing evils. I, the little son, now swear and announce to the spirits of Our Ancestors in Heaven the Fourteen Articles of the Grand Plan, relying on the lasting merits of Our Ancestors to bring them to completion; I will not dare to violate them. May the bright spirits look down and bear witness.

paragraphs.orig: 割斷附依淸國慮念確建自主獨立基礎 制定王室典範以昭大位繼承曁宗戚分義 大君主御正殿視事政務親詢各大臣裁決后嬪宗戚不容干預 王室事務與國政事務須卽分離毋相混合 議政府及各衙門職務權限明行制定 人民出稅總由法令定率不可妄加名目濫行徵收 租稅課徵及經費支出總由度支衙門管轄 王室費用率先減節以爲各衙門及地方官模範 王室費及各官府費用豫定一年額算確立財政基礎 地方官制亟行改定以限節地方官吏職權 國中聰俊子弟廣行派遣以傳習外國學術技藝 敎育將官用徵兵法確定軍制基礎 民法刑法嚴明制定不可濫行監禁懲罰以保全人民生命及財産 用人不拘門地求士遍及朝野以廣人才登庸
paragraphs.en: (1) Cut off the thought of attaching oneself to and relying on Qing China, and firmly establish the foundations of self-rule and independence. (2) Enact a Royal House Code, to make clear the succession to the great throne and the proper duties among royal kin. (3) The Grand Sovereign shall appear in the main hall to attend to affairs, personally consult the various ministers on government business and decide; the queen, consorts and royal kin shall not be allowed to interfere. (4) Affairs of the royal house and affairs of state must be separated at once and not mixed together. (5) The duties and powers of the State Council and the various offices shall be clearly laid down. (6) Taxes paid by the people shall in all cases be fixed at rates set by law; no names or pretexts may be added, nor levies collected arbitrarily. (7) The imposition of taxes and the expenditure of funds shall all be under the control of the Finance Office. (8) Royal household expenses shall be the first to be reduced, to serve as a model for the various offices and for local officials. (9) Royal household expenses and the expenses of the various government offices shall have a yearly budget fixed in advance, so as to establish a foundation for finance. (10) The local official system shall be revised urgently, to limit the powers of local officials. (11) Intelligent youths of the country shall be widely sent abroad to study foreign learning, arts and techniques. (12) Military officers shall be trained and conscription adopted, to fix the foundation of the military system. (13) The civil code and criminal code shall be strictly enacted; confinement and punishment shall not be imposed arbitrarily, so as to protect the lives and property of the people. (14) Persons shall be employed without regard to family status, and talent sought throughout court and country, to widen the recruitment of able men.

review.notes: Kept only the 官報 oath and fourteen articles (dropped the 實錄 duplicate and its headings); card and notes updated. Checked the English line by line against the text, and notes facts (Gojong 1852-1919, Kim Hong-jip, Bak Yeong-hyo 1861-1939 and 1910 marquis title, Inoue, dates, Yu Gil-jun hedged as 'said to'). Script is 'mixed' so no readings are required.
